evidence: WinSCP modal windows appear behind a pinned parent.
The author corrects the original framing: WPF is also affected when Owner is unset, while owned ShowDialog works.
The0.85.1 follow-up says toggling Always On Top brings the hidden modal forward.
Current AlwaysOnTop pins the selected window with SetWindowPos(HWND_TOPMOST); that does not establish an ownership relationship for an unowned modal.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the owner/no-owner contrast and preserve unrelated same-process windows as negative controls.
judgment.rationale: Trace actual owner chains and foreground/topmost transitions. Automatically promoting every same-process window could expose unrelated windows or create persistent topmost state. Unfixed, a hidden blocking modal makes the pinned app appear hung.

prerequisites: WinSCP plus a test-owned WPF app with owned and unowned ShowDialog variants.
A second unrelated same-process window as a negative control.
steps: Pin the parent and open owned then unowned dialogs.
Record owner chain, foreground/topmost and whether the parent is blocked.
Compare toggle behavior and verify cleanup after closing/unpinning.
reproduce.expected: Blocking dialogs remain usable without globally promoting unrelated windows or leaving stale topmost state.
